# 246 — PR explainer (HIGH tier — verifier-assigned; full walkthrough + quiz at the bottom)

**Tier note.** The spec guessed LOW and so did the builder. The verifier reassigned **HIGH** and is
right: the code-relevant diff is 452 lines (`style.css` 11 + `style.min.css` 2 + `package.json` 2 +
`test_card_numeral_wrap.js` 437), over NORTH_STAR's 150-line LOW cap — the same shape as item 245's
precedent. Nothing here touches trust-rail constants, the IA router, parameterized-URL behaviour,
generated SEO surface, config or dependencies; the tier comes from diff size alone, and it is the test
file that carries it. Per NORTH_STAR's risk policy HIGH still auto-merges, but only with this full
explainer and the 5-question quiz below.

**What shipped:** three `white-space: nowrap;` declarations in `style.css` (`.pool-apy-hero`,
`.pool-apy-preview`, `.tvl-value`), the regenerated `style.min.css`, and one new rendered-behaviour
guard, `test_card_numeral_wrap.js`, registered in `test:serial`. No markup, no JS, no tokens, no
geometry, no copy, no translations.

**Why.** Spec 246 batched three C4 findings from `reports/2026-08-06-ux-audit-3screens.md`. That audit
was measured on the **pre-merge 225 branch**; #393/#409/#411/#412/#413 have landed since. Re-measuring
all three on `main` in rendered Chromium (9-pool fixture, both views, both themes, 360/768/1280/1540)
before writing any code changed what the item is:

| Leg | Audit's claim | Measured on `main` today | Shipped |
|-----|---------------|--------------------------|---------|
| (a) `$X.XX/day` wraps to 2 lines | live | **does not reproduce for the non-anomalous majority** (widest string ≈`$27.40/day`, ~70px in a 282px card) — but the string is **unbounded for the anomalous subpopulation** | guard for one subpopulation, real protection for the other |
| (b) "Underlying Assets" chip renders mono-caps | live | **already closed** — `.pool-token-chip` computed `font-family` === body's stack, `text-transform: none` (247's world rewrite; `PoolDetail.js:1049` says so) | pinned by test, no CSS change |
| (c) last row orphans a single card | live | **live** — 9 pools → rows `[4,4,1]` at 1280 and 1540 | **not fixed** (see below) |

But the same re-measurement found the class's still-live member, which the audit had not named: an
**anomaly-flagged APY hero wraps to two lines** — `⚠ 36,452.38%` splitting the warning glyph from the
number it qualifies, in grid view at 1540/1280/360 and list view at 1280/768. That is a trust-rail
legibility defect on the most consequential cell of the card, and it is what `.pool-apy-hero`'s rule
actually repairs.

The other two rules are **not simply pre-emptive** — attempt 1 said they were, and the verifier caught
the overstatement. `getQuickPreview()` (`app.js:2929-2937`) computes `dailyEarnings` from raw
`apyBase + apyReward` with **no clamp**, and `.pool-apy-preview` renders for every non-zero-yield pool
including anomalous ones (`isAnomalousApy()` only swaps the hero's className/glyph; it never suppresses
the `$/day` sibling). So the ≈`$27.40/day` ceiling holds only *below* `APY_SANITY_LIMIT`. The live
snapshot carries **17 anomalous pools of 7,339 (0.23%)** today, the worst (`zeebu`) rendering
**`$10,800.22/day`** — 394× the stated bound, with no ceiling above it. `.pool-apy-preview`'s rule
therefore guards a genuinely unbounded string for that 0.23% and is a durability guard for the other
99.77%; `.tvl-value`'s is a durability guard (`formatCurrency` has no upper bound either).

**Reading order of the diff.** `style.css` §4156 `.tvl-value`, §4170 `.pool-apy-preview`, §4223
`.pool-apy-hero` — one declaration plus a comment naming the positive control in each. No ellipsis or
truncation anywhere: a truncated number would be a trust-rail violation (CLAUDE.md), so a wrap
discipline is the only admissible shape for this fix. `style.min.css` is `npm run minify` output.
`test_card_numeral_wrap.js` derives its population from the **rendered DOM** at test time — every
`.pool-apy-hero` / `.pool-apy-preview` / `.pool-apy-tag` / `.tvl-value` inside every rendered
`.pool-card` — and asserts one-line rendering + computed `white-space: nowrap` per cell, plus no page
or cell overflow, across 16 view × theme × viewport combinations (414 cells scanned), plus the leg-(b)
chip pin. Its overlap check compares each numeral cell against a **derived** neighbour set — every
text-bearing leaf element in the same card, so `.pool-context-inline` and `.pool-symbol` are covered
automatically and so would any future text element be — and its long-name fixture is the **longest
project slug actually present in `data/pools-snapshot.json`**, computed at run time and printed each
run (currently `hamilton-lane-senior-credit-opportunities-securitize-fund`, 57 chars).
`package.json` gains the one registry line `test_test_registry.js` requires.

**The overflow risk was measured, not assumed — and the claim is scoped to what was tested.** List view
lays the row out as `40px 1fr 110px 130px 120px`; a single-line `⚠ 36,452.38%` could have overrun the
110px APY track. It measures `clientWidth === scrollWidth === 110px` at 768/1280/1540 in both themes —
it fits exactly. No track was widened, so the approved list view is untouched and
`test_list_default.js` / `test_list_polish.js` needed no changes (run anyway: 3/3 and 6/6). Attempt 1
claimed "zero overflow and zero overlap **anywhere**"; that is now narrowed to the neighbour set and
fixture population actually exercised — see what the narrowing exposed, below.

**Deviations from the spec, all deliberate.**
1. For the non-anomalous majority leg (a) is a guard, not a repair — the named instance no longer
   reproduces there. The spec's acceptance criterion ("every per-day cell single-line") is met, but it
   was already met before the change for those pools; the honest evidence is the non-vacuity
   transcript, not the green. For the anomalous 0.23% it is a real guard on an unbounded string.
2. Leg (b) ships zero CSS. It was already correct; only the pin is new.
3. **Leg (c) is not fixed and the class is left open, with the number.** An orphan row appears whenever
   `N mod cols == 1`; the grid is `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(280px,1fr))` with `max-width: 1200px` and
   `gap: 12px`, i.e. 3 columns at 1024–1279px and 4 at ≥1280px. Every CSS-only remedy inside the spec's
   own constraints ("no layout recomposition", "no new layout system", no behaviour change) trades a
   benign grid remainder for a worse asymmetry (a full-bleed or double-width last card), and the only
   real fix — making the result count divide by the column count — is a behaviour change the spec
   excludes. Shipping the narrow fix is allowed; claiming it closed the class is not.
4. Open sibling instance recorded, not fixed: `.pool-symbol` wraps to 2–3 lines in **list** view at
   768/360px for long chain-suffixed symbols. It is text, not a numeral cell.
5. **Two pre-existing collisions found while widening the guard, neither introduced nor fixed here**
   (filed as backlog **259**): (i) the longest live project slug paired with an anomalous APY collides
   `.pool-apy-hero` with `.pool-context-inline` at 768px in list view, both themes — reproduced on both
   sides of this item's change, so `nowrap` neither causes nor cures it; (ii) `.tvl-value` at a
   garbage TVL magnitude overlaps `.calculate-yield-btn-new` in grid view at 1280/1540px, surfaced when
   an early draft of the neighbour derivation included interactive controls. The shipped derivation
   excludes `.pool-cta-section` deliberately and says so in the test's header — the exclusion is
   recorded, not silent, precisely so it cannot launder (ii).

**Non-vacuity.** Each of the three rules was deleted separately → the suite went red naming that exact
cell → restored → green, with `md5sum` proving a byte-identical restore; the leg-(b) pin was reddened
by temporarily adding `text-transform: uppercase` to `.pool-token-chip`. Two traps were hit and
recorded rather than papered over: `home.html` loads `style.min.css`, so every trial needs a re-minify
(the first pass produced a false green), and realistic TVL/$-per-day magnitudes cannot stress those two
tracks at all, so the fixture gained two garbage-magnitude pools — grounded, not invented:
`getQuickPreview`'s `$/day` is **not** clamped to `APY_SANITY_LIMIT` and `formatCurrency` has no upper
bound, which is RAZOR.md worked example 2's exact shape. Full transcript: `specs/246-notes.md`.

**Class statement.** A wrap defect in a different numeral cell of a pool card is caught automatically —
the scan is a population scan, not an instance list — and after attempt 2 a *collision* with a
different neighbouring text element is caught too, because the neighbour set is derived from the
rendered card rather than enumerated. Outside `.pool-card` nothing is covered: the planner, the
pool-detail page body and the generated token/chain pages render their own numerals under other classes
and are not guarded. Two boundaries remain inside the card: the four-class numeral enumeration is finite
(a genuinely new numeral element under a new class name needs adding to `NUMERAL_CLASSES`), and the
neighbour derivation excludes `.pool-cta-section`, so numeral-vs-control collisions — deviation 5(ii) —
are outside it by construction.

**Why this is not gated by the 2026-08-05 DESIGN QUALITY BAR** (the 2026-08-10 run deferred 246 on
those grounds, and this run overrides that with reasoning rather than silently): that directive governs
the visual-world increments — screenshot-first design passes, each human-approved before the next. This
diff changes no token, no colour, no type scale, no spacing, no geometry and no component structure; it
stops a warning glyph from being orphaned from its number. It is a legibility/trust-rail repair, not a
design increment. The two legs of 246 that *were* design work (the chip restyle and the grid
recomposition) are precisely the two this PR does not perform — one because 247 already did it, one
because it is left open. If the human reads that differently, the revert is three lines.
